body:
I did some digging into the source code and here are my findings.
In my example unsafe fraction is 0.25 which is exact distance needed for bodies to touch each other but not overlap.
After unsafe fraction is calculated shape is moved to colliding position in this line:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/394508d26dcf1b7a9362453f9009c07d969f1a7e/scene/2d/physics/shape_cast_2d.cpp#L318
We can see that `CMP_EPSILON` is added to motion vector to make sure that body is actually intersecting and not just touching.
Then `rest_info()` is called to check if there are any collisions in new position:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/394508d26dcf1b7a9362453f9009c07d969f1a7e/scene/2d/physics/shape_cast_2d.cpp#L329
But it seems like adding `CMP_EPSILON` may just not be enough for `rest_info()` to actually find a collision. So let's see how `unsafe` is calculated in comparsion to `rest_info()`. Ideally these two should just be consistent and no additional `CMP_EPSILON` should be needed.
`unsafe` is calculated using binary search and `GodotCollisionSolver2D::solve()`. Here's the code: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/394508d26dcf1b7a9362453f9009c07d969f1a7e/modules/godot_physics_2d/godot_space_2d.cpp#L306
`rest_info()` seems to use the same method:
`https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/394508d26dcf1b7a9362453f9009c07d969f1a7e/modules/godot_physics_2d/godot_space_2d.cpp#L477
So I see few possibilities:
- Maybe parameters passed to `solve()` in both cases does not match so they give different results. This is actually true because when calculating `unsafe` wo do not use this `CMP_EPSILON` component. So parameters actually are different. But it should rather help if anything.
- There is this additional condition in `rest_info()` that seem to reject collisions in some cases. I haven't dig further to understand it. https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/394508d26dcf1b7a9362453f9009c07d969f1a7e/modules/godot_physics_2d/godot_space_2d.cpp#L483

Anyway. It should be somehow ensured that `unsafe` and later `rest_info()` are calculated in consistent way. Maybe `cast_motion()` should return more verbose response. Not just a fraction but set of parameters to be later used for `solve()` method to find actual collisions.
